items.title: Rupee remains stable at 95.37 ahead of RBI policy
items.description: The Indian rupee closed nearly unchanged on Tuesday, trading within a narrow band. Importer hedging demand and FPI inflows supported the currency's stability. Caution ahead of the monetary policy announcement also influenced its movement. Brent crude prices remained between eighty and eighty-three dollars per barrel. The rupee settled at ninety-five point thirty-seven against the dollar.

items.title: Higher funding costs, rising competition may weigh on Muthoot Finance
items.description: Muthoot Finance shares dropped nearly eight percent after reporting lower net interest margins. Loan yields are expected to remain under pressure this year due to rising costs. Earnings growth in FY27 will depend on loan book expansion, not margin improvement. The company's stock has seen a nineteen percent decline since mid-May. Analysts anticipate moderated earnings growth for Muthoot Finance over coming years.

items.title: Stocks in news: BSE, PB Fintech, Nykaa, Airtel, and LIC
items.description: Markets experienced profit-taking after Monday's rally, with indices closing lower. Investors await the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy announcement on Wednesday. BSE reported a significant profit increase for the June quarter, driven by revenue growth. Bharti Airtel and Nykaa also announced strong quarterly earnings, showing substantial profit jumps. The government began an offer for sale in LIC for non-retail investors.

items.title: REITs, publicly-listed InvITs may get to raise foreign capital via DRs
items.description: Sebi proposed allowing real estate and infrastructure trusts to raise foreign capital.  This move aims to broaden foreign investor access to India's investment trust market.  Depository receipts will enable trading in foreign currency on international exchanges.  Privately listed infrastructure trusts will not be eligible for this new facility.  The proposal seeks to attract more global capital into these investment vehicles.

items.title: LIC's OFS discount looks tempting, but triggers don't
items.description: Analysts hold differing views on retail investor interest in LIC's offer for sale. The government is divesting a stake to meet minimum public shareholding norms. Some analysts cite attractive valuations and discounted pricing for participation. Others caution about the absence of immediate upside triggers for the insurer. The offer aims to comply with regulatory requirements and potentially reduce the government's stake.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Domestic markets saw profit booking after recent gains, with the Nifty declining slightly. Indian equities are expected to see a gradual upmove, supported by global cues and earnings. Investors will monitor US jobs data and the RBI's monetary policy decision tomorrow. The India VIX, a fear gauge, rose to 12.19 levels. The rupee appreciated nine paise against the US dollar on Tuesday.

items.title: Closing auction keeps traders on edge as divergence persists
items.description: Market participants faced confusion with the new closing auction system on Tuesday. This system change affected the determination of official stock closing prices. The expiry of Nifty weekly futures and options contracts added to market complexity. Traders reported unexpected derivative price movements and position losses. The Sensex and Nifty experienced divergence for a second consecutive day.

items.title: IRDAI asks insurers to fast-track Assam flood claims
items.description: Insurers must expedite flood claim settlements for affected policyholders. The regulator has directed immediate deployment of surveyors and loss assessors. Special district-level claims desks and 24x7 helplines will be established. Electronic communication is encouraged to speed up claim registration and payments. This directive follows heavy rains and floods which began on July 19.

items.title: Microfinance lending dips as uneven monsoon alters the landscape
items.description: India's microfinance sector contracted in the first quarter after a previous rebound. Uneven monsoon progress weighed on rural demand and lender caution grew. The sector's portfolio shrank four percent to ₹3.26 lakh crore by June end. Business usually slows during this period, but rainfall added concerns. Lenders remain cautious about growing loans due to uncertain patterns.

items.title: Nykaa shares dip 3% despite multifold jump in Q1 profit; analysts weigh in
items.description: Nykaa operator FSN E-Commerce Ventures saw its shares fall despite a strong Q1 FY27 performance. Consolidated net profit more than tripled to Rs 80 crore, while revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs 2,782 crore.

items.title: Bharti Airtel shares jump 4% after Q1 results. Here’s what Jefferies, CLSA, others are saying
items.description: Bharti Airtel shares rose 4% after the telecom major reported a 37% year-on-year jump in June-quarter net profit and an 18% increase in revenue. Brokerages remained bullish, with target prices implying up to 21% upside, driven by strong subscriber additions, higher ARPU and robust cash flows.

items.title: Canara Bank, Bank of Baroda among 7 bank stocks with up to 26% upside potential. Own any?
items.description: Domestic brokerage firm ICICI Securities has initiated coverage on seven public sector banks. The brokerage said the phase of strong earnings growth and return on assets (RoA) expansion for PSU banks appears to be losing momentum. Even so, it expects return on equity (RoE) to remain healthy at around 15% during FY27 and FY28, while noting that valuations for most PSU banks remain below their FY28 RoA, providing valuation comfort. Here’s the full list.

items.title: Why is market rising today? Sensex jumps over 400 pts, Nifty above 24,600. 8 factors behind D-St rebound
items.description: The Indian stock market saw a rebound on Wednesday, with Sensex and Nifty 50 trading higher. Easing oil prices and strong foreign institutional investor buying boosted investor sentiment significantly. Bharti Airtel and IndiGo shares led the gains, while Titan experienced a slight decline. Broader markets also performed well, with midcap and smallcap indices showing gains. Several sectors contributed to the positive movement, with realty leading the advance.

items.title: Kalyan Jewellers slips 3% as Q1 margin pressure overshadows 32% jump in net profit
items.description: Kalyan Jewellers shares fell 3% after its June-quarter results highlighted margin pressure despite strong earnings growth. Consolidated net profit rose 32% year-on-year to Rs 348.7 crore, while revenue surged 45.7% to Rs 10,588.9 crore. Investors remained cautious as higher gold exchange volumes and promotional offers weighed on margins, offsetting the retailer's robust sales performance.

items.title: H.R. Hygiene Products shares to list today on BSE SME. Here’s what GMP suggests
items.description: H.R. Hygiene Products is set to debut on the BSE SME platform today after its IPO was subscribed 6.26 times. Ahead of the listing, the grey market premium (GMP) stands at Re 1, indicating a modest 1% listing gain over the upper issue price of Rs 88. The company plans to use the IPO proceeds to set up a new manufacturing facility in Gujarat, repay borrowings and meet general corporate requirements. Investors will also track the company's financial performance and market response after the listing.

items.title: Buy, Sell or Hold: Nuvama maintains a buy on NYKAA and Uno Minda; Elara Securities recommends buy on Godrej Properties
items.description: Brokerages remain bullish on select consumer, auto component, and real estate stocks. Nuvama reiterated 'Buy' on Nykaa (target Rs 414) and Uno Minda (target raised to Rs 1,380) citing margin expansion and strong demand, while Elara Securities maintained 'Buy' on Godrej Properties (target Rs 3,200), seeing 57% upside.

items.title: 5 Nifty stocks trading at significant discounts of up to 36% to historical averages. How many do you have?
items.description: After a volatile year for Indian equities, several Nifty 50 stocks are now trading at significant discounts to their historical valuation averages. While the correction reflects concerns amid geopolitical worries, experts believe the sharp derating has created attractive opportunities for long term investors.

items.title: BSE shares fall 2% despite 62% jump in Q1 net profit to Rs 874 crore. Should you buy, sell or hold?
items.description: BSE reported a significant 62% profit jump and 63% revenue increase for the first quarter.  Investment income also saw a sharp rise during the reported period.  Analysts maintained positive calls but reduced price targets due to regulatory changes.  Industry volumes declined, impacting profit estimates for upcoming financial years.  BSE shares experienced a slight decline after the financial results were announced.

items.title: PVR Inox among 5 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On August 4, five Nifty500 stocks that gained over 4% appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: Saregama India among 4 stocks closed above VWAP, signalling bullish shift
items.description: On August 4, the closing prices of four stocks in the Nifty500 pack rallied more than 2% above their VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price), according to StockEdge's technical scan data. A move above the VWAP indicates that the closing price was higher than the average price at which the stock traded during the session, weighted by trading volume.This is widely interpreted by traders and investors as a bullish signal, suggesting stronger buying interest and positive market sentiment.

items.title: KEI Industries among 6 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On 4 August, six Nifty500 stocks that gained over 2 per cent were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from stockedge.com. It is an uptrend signal if the RSI value has crossed above 50 from below. "RSI trending up" means that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are increasing, suggesting strengthening momentum in the price of the stock. This can indicate potential upward movement and may be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: Inside LIC’s Rs 16 lakh crore portfolio: Its biggest stock buys and sells in June quarter
items.description: Life Insurance Corporation bought shares worth over Rs 16,000 crore in June.  Bharti Airtel and Maruti Suzuki saw the largest buying from the insurer.  LIC also sold shares worth over Rs 13,000 crore during this period.  Its overall market share declined to an all-time low despite net buying.  Financial services remained the largest sector exposure for LIC's portfolio.

items.title: LIC OFS opens for retail investors: Should you apply in insurance behemoth's offer?
items.description: The OFS opened for non-retail investors on August 4, and saw strong participation. The offer was oversubscribed more than 3 times its offer size. It now opens for retail investors today.

items.title: Manipal Health Enterprises shares to list today; GMP indicates flat debut
items.description: The company's IPO is currently commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of around Rs 3, or nearly 1% over the upper price band of Rs 590 per share, indicating an estimated listing price of Rs 593. While the GMP is widely tracked as a gauge of investor sentiment, it is an unofficial and unregulated indicator and should not be considered a reliable predictor of listing-day performance.

items.title: Stocks to buy in 2026 for long term: M&M, UPL among 5 stocks that could 10-20% return
